A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments, image and video interpolation evaluations, guidance correction, distillation results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime measurements and an optimization-budget analysis in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The score-Jacobian metric, geodesic energy minimization, DDIM interpolation pipeline, and single-step conjugate-gradient guidance correction remain unchanged. Revised explanations and notation do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic distribution, MorphBench subsets, Animal Faces-HQ, CelebA-HQ, DAVIS, Human, RE10K, MS-COCO, and Conceptual 12M. The added runtime and iteration-budget evaluations use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain LERP, SLERP, NAO, NoiseDiff, GeoDiff, and the FIM-based metric for interpolation, and CFG/CFG++ for guidance. The new computational analysis reuses existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 adds end-to-end timing per MB(A) image pair on one RTX A6000 and a DAVIS evaluation varying geodesic optimization budgets in 100-iteration increments. Existing benchmark protocols and the default 500-iteration interpolation budget are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused computational analysis: Table E.4 compares runtime, and Figure E.2 tests how geodesic optimization iterations affect DAVIS MSE. Existing prompt-adjustment, noise-level, spectral-gap, backbone, and guidance-solver analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the one-sided exact binomial tests, significance thresholds, five matched-seed distillation runs, and spectral median/quantile/range reporting. Changed significance markers are result changes, without a documented change in statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table E.4 adds runtimes of 178.29, 216.79, and 392.92 seconds for FIM-based, GeoDiff, and Ours; Figure E.2 adds iteration-dependent MSE results. Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged, but Ours' MB(M) PPL and CA reconstruction-error markers in Table 2, and DAVIS LPIPS marker in Table 3, change from ** to *. Figure E.1 also adds a MorphBench animation example.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects the claim that a nonsymmetric Jacobian's right singular vectors need not be orthogonal, replacing 'right singular vectors' with 'eigenvectors.' Appendix E.3 also explicitly describes the scaled-identity Jacobian and rescaled Euclidean metric in the ideal Gaussian limit. The central metric and proposition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same training-free metric contribution, interpolation and guidance claims, and distillation benefit. The introduction clarifies attribution of the spectral insight without changing the scientific scope of these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains why input-dependent DDIM-inverted endpoints can retain a residual spectral gap near maximum noise, beyond v2's explanation through increasing isotropy. It also explains the measured runtime overhead through backpropagation and makes the roughly 1.8-times-GeoDiff cost–quality tradeoff explicit.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents measured end-to-end interpolation costs with their per-pair, dataset, hardware, and experimental-setting context in Appendix E.3. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, distillation, and hardware disclosures are otherwise retained; repeated setup details in the main text are not new settings.

R1.justification: The introduction more explicitly attributes the tangent–normal characterization to prior observations. References to Hu et al.'s LoRA paper, Changpinyo et al.'s Conceptual 12M paper, and Calvin Luo's diffusion tutorial are removed, although LoRA and Conceptual 12M remain used. The main related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify attribution, interpolation notation, and experimental descriptions. Explanations from Figures 3–4 are moved and expanded into Appendix B.2; acknowledgements and author contact details are added, and citations become numeric. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document undergoes a substantial typesetting and layout redesign, including typography, margins, headings, table styling, and float placement. Algorithms are paired with their diagrams, and the existing dog comparison moves from the appendix into Figure 5. New runtime and iteration-budget displays and an additional qualitative panel accompany the extensive reformatting.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical precision through the Appendix B.1 correction and practical transparency through measured runtime and optimization-budget evidence in Appendix E.3. The new analysis exposes the cost–quality tradeoff that v2's asymptotic comparison left unclear. These limited gains outweigh the loss of a few supporting citations; the central method and benchmark conclusions remain unchanged.
